extracted.intended_audience: care provider facilities, PRS providers, and ORR program administrators (and stakeholders providing public comment)
extracted.subtask_short: ORR care facility standards for unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory standards and operational requirements that care provider facilities and post-release service (PRS) providers must meet when caring for unaccompanied children in ORR custody or under ORR-funded programs, including privacy, monitoring, service delivery, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS privacy protections and information-sharing controls
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must have a written policy and procedure that protects sensitive information of released unaccompanied children from access by unauthorized users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include encrypting electronic communication (email, text messaging) containing sensitive healthcare or identifying information; explaining to released children and sponsors how, when, and under what circumstances sensitive information may be shared; and implementing appropriate controls on information sharing within the PRS provider network to prevent exploitation by unauthorized users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) — when to report
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers concerned about an unaccompanied child's safety and well-being must document and report a Notification of Concern (NOC) to ORR and, as applicable, other investigative agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations anticipated to require a NOC include emergencies; current human trafficking; abuse, abandonment, neglect, maltreatment; possible exploitative employment; kidnapping, disappearance, runaway; alleged criminal activity; child protection services involvement; potential fraud (e.g., document fraud, improper fees); behavioral incidents raising safety concern; media attention; sponsor declining services; contact with organized crime; inability to contact the child within 30 days of release; or loss of contact with safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) — timeframe and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PRS providers must submit a NOC to ORR within 24 hours of first knowledge or suspicion of events raising concerns about the child's safety and well-being and must document the NOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must both report to relevant agencies (e.g., law enforcement, child protective services) as applicable and maintain documentation of the NOC submission and underlying facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case closure procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A case file must be formally closed when PRS are terminated by ORR, following ORR-supplied instructions and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, providers may be required to complete a case closure form and upload it to ORR's online case management system within 72 hours of case closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensure and compliance with state/federal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must be licensed by an appropriate state or Federal agency, or meet other ORR-specified requirements if state licensure is unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard programs must comply with applicable state child welfare laws and state/local building, fire, health and safety codes. If ORR requirements exceed state law, providers should comply with both where possible; ORR will review conflicts. ORR employees must follow federal duties in case of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of proper physical care and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide or arrange for necessary physical care and maintenance for each child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes suitable living accommodations, food, drinking water, appropriate clothing, personal grooming and hygiene items, access to toilets and sinks, adequate temperature control and ventilation, and adequate supervision to protect children from others. Food must be of adequate variety, quality, and quantity per USDA Dietary Guidelines for Americans and appropriate for child/activity level; drinking water must always be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized needs assessment upon intake
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unaccompanied child must receive an individualized needs assessment that gathers identification and history and identifies special or immediate needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment components: initial intake forms; biographic and family data; history (migration, health, substance use, mental health); identification of special needs or immediate intervention needs; education assessment and plan; language needs (e.g., indigenous language speaker); assessment of family relationships and interactions; religious preference; personal goals, strengths, weaknesses; contact information for family/relatives/friends who may assist in release. ORR solicits comment on substituting 'individualized needs' for 'special needs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Education services and effective communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide education services appropriate to the child's development, communication skills, and disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education must be in a structured classroom Monday–Friday, focus primarily on basic academic competencies (science, social studies, math, reading, writing, physical education) and secondarily on English Language Training, include materials/instruction in needed languages, provide reading materials in other languages for leisure, and ensure effective communication for children with disabilities (auxiliary aids/services per 45 CFR 85.51 such as interpreters, Braille, audio, note-takers). Additional staffing requirements referenced in §410.1305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreation and leisure time requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must have a recreation and leisure time plan to support health and well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must include daily outdoor activity (weather permitting), at least one hour per day of large muscle activity, and one hour per day of structured leisure-time activities (excluding television). On days when school is not in session, activities must total at least three hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling and mental health supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide counseling and mental health supports, including individual and group counseling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require at least one individual counseling session per week conducted by certified counseling staff to review progress, set objectives, and address developmental/crisis needs. Group counseling must be provided at least twice a week and may be informal; sessions may include program management discussion and should avoid pressuring children to disclose private issues. Additional mental health and substance use disorder treatment provided based on need, including specialized care and in-person or virtual options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acculturation and adaptation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs must provide acculturation and adaptation services to develop social and interpersonal skills necessary for independent and responsible living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services should support social development and cultural needs of children in standard programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission procedures and initial care upon arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon admission, standard programs must address immediate needs and conduct an initial intake assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate needs: food, hydration, personal hygiene, clean clothing and bedding. Initial intake must cover biographic, family, migration, health, substance use, and mental health history. If trafficking or labor exploitation is indicated, care provider must notify the ACF Office of Trafficking in Persons within 24 hours. Programs must provide comprehensive orientation (written and oral) in accessible formats and languages the child understands about program intent, services, rules, availability of legal assistance, immigration/employment info, Ombuds services, and assist with contacting family per ORR guidance. Medical needs assessed per §410.1307. Orientation re sexual abuse/harassment per existing §411.33 and 45 CFR part 411 subpart E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural, religious, and spiritual accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide for cultural, religious, and spiritual needs whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access to religious services of the child's choice; celebrate culture-specific events/holidays; be culturally aware in daily activities, food menus, clothing, and hygiene routines; incorporate cultures into educational services. Operate in compliance with RFRA, federal conscience protections, civil rights laws, and HHS regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitation and contact with family
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide structured visitation and contact with family members to encourage regular contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least 15 minutes of phone or video contact three times a week (parents/legal guardians, other family/caregivers, domestic or abroad) in a private space ensuring confidentiality at no cost. This is the minimum; programs may provide more (e.g., daily calls). Encourage in-person visitation unless documented safety concerns and have policies to ensure safety/privacy (e.g., alternative public visit place).

rubrics_metrics.name: Family unification services
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must assist with family unification services to facilitate safe and timely release to sponsors or relatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance includes identifying and verifying relatives in the U.S. and foreign countries and helping to obtain legal guardianship if necessary for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on legal rights and legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide unaccompanied children with information about legal services and rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include availability of free legal assistance, right to representation by counsel at no expense to government, right to a removal hearing before an immigration judge, ability to apply for asylum with USCIS, and ability to request voluntary departure instead of removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on child labor laws and permissible work
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must provide information about U.S. child labor laws and permissible work opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information and education should be sensitive to the age, culture, and native language of each child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culturally competent delivery of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Services required in §410.1302(c) must be delivered in a manner sensitive to age, culture, native language, and complex needs of each child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes cultural competency as a program component consistent with the FSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual service planning and case management
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must develop comprehensive, realistic individual service plans based on the individualized needs assessment and coordinate implementation through case management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should identify individualized, person-centered goals with measurable outcomes and steps; be developed with child input; reviewed/updated at regular intervals (current practice: every 30 days); children aged 14+ should receive a copy (younger children when appropriate); plans must be in the child's native language or provided via auxiliary aids/services, use clear, concise language and visual aids, and include checks for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring activities and types
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR will monitor care provider facilities for compliance using multiple monitoring activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring includes desk monitoring (ongoing HQ oversight: monthly check-ins, records/report reviews, financial/budget analysis, staff background check reviews, communications review), routine site visits (day-long, typically once or twice monthly, announced/unannounced), site visits in response to reports or investigations, and routine monitoring visits (week-long comprehensive reviews, typically at least every two years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: When out of compliance, ORR will issue corrective actions and specify timeframes and disciplinary consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will communicate concerns in writing with a list of corrective actions and child welfare best practice recommendations, request a response, and specify timeframes. Disciplinary consequences can include stopping placements until corrective actions are addressed or potential non-renewal of grants; ORR may initiate a Graduated Corrective Action Plan with increasing reporting and oversight for persistent non-compliance (see §410.1307(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional monitoring for secure facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure facilities are subject to additional monitoring activities including review of individual case files for placement reassessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will review case files to ensure children placed in secure facilities are assessed at least every 30 days for the possibility of transfer to a less restrictive setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring long-term and transitional home care
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term and transitional foster care homes are subject to monitoring tailored to foster care arrangements and must monitor sub-recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-site monitoring may include first-hand assessment of home environment and oversight; long-term/transitional providers must conduct annual monitoring/site visits of sub-recipients and weekly desk monitoring, and must provide findings to the designated ORR point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance assessment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must develop QA assessment procedures to accurately measure and evaluate service delivery compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA procedures should measure compliance with requirements of part 410 and applicable provisions of 45 CFR part 411.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting standards and prohibited uses of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must report emergency incidents, significant incidents, or program-level events to ORR and applicable authorities and document incidents in a trauma-informed, accurate manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must include sufficient detail for follow-up, be trauma-informed and grounded in child welfare best practices, and be updated with later findings. Facilities must never fabricate, exaggerate, or minimize incidents; use disparaging or judgmental language; or use incident reporting or threats of reporting to manage behavior or for other illegitimate reasons. ORR prohibits using reports of significant incidents as punishment, as sole basis for stepping a child up to more restrictive placement, refusing to step a child down, or refusing a placement (reports may be cited as examples of concerning behavior but cannot alone justify those actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality, ownership, and access to case file records
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities and PRS providers must develop, maintain, and safeguard individual case file records of unaccompanied children; such records are ORR property and subject to strict disclosure controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be protected from unauthorized use/disclosure. Providers may not release case file records or information for purposes other than program administration without prior ORR approval. Providers and PRS must provide case files immediately upon ORR request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on employee/contractor disclosures and pre-approved limited disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees, former employees, or contractors must not disclose case file records or information except for program administration without advance notice to ORR; ORR pre-approves certain limited disclosures for efficient administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may pre-approve limited disclosures for school registration and routine educational purposes, routine medical/dental/mental health treatment, emergency medical care, obtaining services per ORR policies, and disclosures pursuant to whistleblower protection laws. Requests for case file information must be made directly to ORR so ORR can consider safety/privacy and compatibility with statutory program goals and laws.
